llm.pacing_note: Run 34002128822 showed four concurrent shards each rejected after ~5 requests with "Please retry in 3.9-38.9s" while the aggregate was only ~4 requests/minute, so the usable free-tier allowance is far below the advertised 20/min. Waits stay bounded and one shared per-process event budget stops the job instead of grinding the quota away.
llm.role: audits drafts, audits negatives, repairs references and grades answers; independent of the candidate

quota_policy: Checkpoint every response and completed case. Pause and ask the user before changing provider/credential profile; never silently replay another model as Qwen.
reference_policy: Original PDF page images and logical DOCX text define draft references; runtime extraction stays unchanged for the agent. Freeze separate answer keys before prediction. Model-authored/audited keys are not expert-certified.

candidate_llm.note: User approved answering on qwen via XKIRO_API_KEY with the JINKO key as the alternate credential; the harness gate still refuses any non-Qwen candidate model, so a Google answer would need a plan change, not a silent fallback.

google_scope: Unfinished reference authoring and auditing only; restore candidate_llm for answering unless the user explicitly approves a further switch.
quota_note: Run 34002128822: shards 4/5/7 were each rejected by Google after ~5 requests (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, limit: 20, "Please retry in 3.9-38.9s") at ~4 requests/minute in aggregate, while the single shard that had already passed its gate kept working. The reference audit is therefore capped at two workers, with a shared per-process event budget that stops a job from grinding the quota. Authoring itself now uses xKiro Qwen, per user choice, and remains labelled as candidate-model-authored reference drafting.

author_llm.role: drafts the paired family; the same model as the candidate, so authoring alone is not validation

scale_note: Frozen version is the scaled retry: 100 supported families per language (300 questions) sampled deterministically from the accepted pool, preferring families whose gold text exists in docs/ and balancing subtype and question style, at 640-token chunks. The 1,000-per-language target and the 200 out-of-scope / 50 insufficient-evidence / 50 adversarial categories stay open: no negative family has ever been authored, so nothing here measures refusal behaviour end to end.

authoring.why: Authoring runs on xKiro Qwen; the reference audit runs on Google, whose free tier measured ~1-2 usable requests/minute. Drafting everything first means a run is never blocked by the scarce provider, and each run still promotes as many audits as the current allowance permits.
authoring.prompt_note: Run 34003690682: shards 6-8 spent 307/331 requests on replies that failed JSON parsing (Expecting ',' delimiter) and accepted nothing, because an abstain family must return prose with quotes and an empty evidence list. The prompt now forbids double quotes inside string values, caps reference_answer length, and states that an empty sources list is intentional for negatives; a shard also stops after 12 unparsable replies instead of spending the whole budget, and reports status blocked_format rather than a deadline.

audit_independence_note: Accepted families 0-469 were audited by the same model that drafted them (cross_provider_audited 0). Role profiles now separate the providers, so families authored from this revision on are drafted by xKiro Qwen and audited by Google; the snapshot manifest and the frozen dataset manifest carry the counts and the report prints them as a caveat. A same-model audit is not described as independent anywhere.
negative_priority_note: All 469 accepted families are supported ones. The 200 out-of-scope and 50 insufficient-evidence families sit in shards 6-8, which were never reached, so the author matrix is ordered least-progressed-first and the scaled freeze is refused until those categories are filled.
shard_order_note: The plan job orders the author matrix least-progressed-first from the committed snapshot manifest, so the untouched negative families in shards 6-8 are authored before the supported shards that already have 100 each. Values are plain integers: object matrix entries bound matrix.shard to the whole object and failed every shard in setup (run 34003466393).

chunking.why: Measured on the same 100x3 sample with no answer model: at 640-token chunks the embedding arm put the full gold span in the top 5 for 82.3% of questions (68.3% at rank 1, abstention AUC 0.798, 96.3% recall on queries sharing no content word), against 11.3% at the pinned 220 where 37% of queries have no chunk holding any part of their evidence. Overlap is unchanged.
chunking.note: config.CHUNK_SIZE_TOKENS stays 220 for the main application; this pin is a hard-harness dataset-version property applied by predict.runtime_config() to every corpus in the harness.

provider_mix_note: Answering is xKiro Qwen only. Reference-side roles may run on Google under the existing free-tier pacing; every published count is labelled with the provider that produced it, so a mixed-provider run is never reported as a Qwen-only number. Answering is xKiro Qwen; grading since revision 26 is experiential/glm-5.3-flash. Every published row and aggregate carries provider/model, and no mixed-provider number is ever reported as a Qwen-only result.
dataset_manifest_note: Frozen in run 34026077962: 100 questions per language (300), sample 100 families drawn from a 476-family pool of which 315 have gold text present in docs/, at 640/40 chunking. source_runtime_manifest above is that run's recomputed fingerprint, so the candidate path accepts the corpus this dataset version was designed against.
answer_run_note: Answering runs on xKiro qwen/qwen3.8-max:free via XKIRO_API_KEY (alternate alias XKIRO_API_KEY_JINKO). Predictions never see answer_key files; grading compares them afterwards.
grading_resume_note: Run 34026369379 answered 300/300 questions on qwen/qwen3.8-max:free at 640-token chunks and graded 82 before Google free tier returned HTTP 429 (limit: 20/min on gemini-3.5-flash). Every grader response is cached, so this phase resumes from the 82 rather than re-spending them; the pause is recorded as provider_pause, never as an answer score.
answer_contract_note: Run 34028010045 paused in the grader calibration before classifying anything. Re-grading the SAME 300 cached predictions costs no answer-model calls and will now report why each reply was rejected by the output contract, because the validator message and a truncated copy of the reply travel into the grading row. This phase is diagnostic; it is not a score.
grading_state_note: 94 of 300 rows classified so far (69 correct, 3 partial, 12 over_refusal, 10 rejected by the output contract), score 0.734 over the scored subset: ar 0.833, fr 0.688, en 0.688. This is a partial measurement of a resumable phase, not the dataset score: 206 comparisons still need the grader, and every completed one is cached and replayed rather than re-requested. Nothing here is reported as final until graded_questions equals 300 with status complete.

grader_llm.role: semantic comparison of answered questions against the frozen answer key
grader_llm.why: The answer model must not grade itself. Google is the only other approved judge and its free-tier per-minute ceiling left 206 of 300 comparisons unscored across three resumes. The user supplied EXPERIENTIAL_API_KEY and named glm-5.3-flash, an OpenAI-compatible catalog slug on the Experiential Labs gateway (api.experientiallabs.ai/v1).
grader_llm.contract: Gateway docs: one Authorization: Bearer header, model named by bare slug, and the smallest body - temperature/top_p/response_format are never sent because a route that rejects them answers all_routes_failed (502), for which the adapter retries once without max_tokens. GLM-5.3-Flash thinks before it writes, so max_tokens is generous and a reply with reasoning but no answer text is refused rather than graded.
grader_llm.billing: Not a free tier: routed tokens are billed per token against account credits. Estimated remaining spend for 206 comparisons at ~6 per request and ~10k tokens per request is a few cents at published GLM-5.3-Flash rates ($0.15/M in, $0.50/M out).
grader_llm.grading_state: Run 34030906572 graded 186 new comparisons on experiential/glm-5.3-flash in 33 requests with no quota pause, taking the sample from 94 to 208 of 300 rows (155 correct, 31 partial, 12 over_refusal, 10 rejected by the output contract; 0.745 over scored rows). It then stopped because the judge covered one batch twice-ish rather than once each: that is now isolated by halving the ask, and a comparison the judge cannot answer becomes grade=judge_unusable, excluded from every score. Cached judgments replay, so this resumes at 208 rather than re-buying them.
